testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How often should you test the low pressure warning signal?
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system charges, test it by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air from the braking system. The warning signal should come on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: What can a modulating control valve control?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets the driver apply spring brakes slowly and smoothly. On equipped vehicles, a lever on the dashboard controls the valve.

questions.question: What part between an air compressor and reservoir tank prevents air from escaping if the compressor leaks?
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is required between an air compressor and the first main reservoir. It stops air from escaping the system if the air compressor leaks.

questions.question: What does the air compressor do on a truck with air brakes?

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls the compressor.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake on newer vehicles?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.
Push in the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Pull up on the steering column.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
questions.explanation: On newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake uses a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes. Push it in to release the brakes.

questions.question: How do you make a normal stop in a vehicle with air brakes?

options.text: Pull out the air brake knob.

questions.explanation: To make a normal stop in a vehicle with air brakes, press the brake pedal down.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake in a newer vehicle?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: On newer vehicles with air brakes, pull the yellow, diamond-shaped knob outward to apply the parking brakes. Push the knob inward to release them.

questions.question: What should you do when traveling down a steep hill?

options.text: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
Keep downshifting instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep hills, use engine braking to control your speed. Use your brakes only when needed to help with engine braking.

questions.question: What shows you how much pressure is in your air tanks?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. It shows the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are activated, what should you never do?

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.
Open the door to the cab.

questions.explanation: Never use the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. Using both springs and air pressure together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a front brake limiting valve, where should you set the control?

options.text: Keep it at the halfway mark.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with two settings: normal and slippery. This valve was designed to reduce brake pressure on slippery surfaces. However, research shows this is not necessary. Always keep the control in the normal position.

questions.question: During an emergency stop using controlled braking, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Press the brakes with about half your normal force.
Press the brakes so the wheels lock.
Press the brakes with very light pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pressing the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Make small steering movements when braking this way.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.explanation: When properly used and maintained, air brakes are safe and effective for stopping large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: What does an application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being used on the brakes right now.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being used on the brakes right now.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows the air pressure being applied to the brakes at this moment. This gauge helps drivers notice if their brakes are starting to wear out.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being used on the brakes right now.
The temperature of the air in the brake system.
The pressure of air coming from the compressor.
The number of times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being used on the brakes right now.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows the air pressure being applied to the brakes at this moment. Not all vehicles with air brakes have this gauge.

questions.question: What does the service brake system do?

options.text: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.
Applies and releases the parking brakes.
Applies and releases the emergency brakes.
Applies and releases the axle brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate parts: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system. The service brake system controls the brakes when you use the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: While driving, what holds spring brakes in place?
questions.explanation: Air pressure keeps spring brakes in place while you drive. If the air pressure drops too low, the springs will engage the brakes automatically.

questions.question: What must truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997, and other air brake vehicles built on or after March 1, 1998, must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks that have manual drains?
questions.explanation: Air tanks with manual drains should be drained at the end of each driving day.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, how much air should leak from a single vehicle with air brakes in one minute?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 2 psi of pressure in one minute during a static leakage test. If it leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube used to move air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes when used
A part within the braking unit that allows air to move freely

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into your view when air pressure in the tanks falls below 60 psi.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle unattended:

options.text: The parking brake must always be used.
The parking brake should never be used.
Windows in the cab should be lowered.

questions.correctAnswerText: The parking brake must always be used.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: To use the controlled braking method, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Apply the brakes with about half-force.
Apply the brakes until the wheels lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means applying the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. If you need to steer while braking, release the brake pedal, steer, then apply the brakes again.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator is especially important:
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, once air pressure is lost and the spring brakes come on:

options.text: You will be unable to move the vehicle.
A separate air tank can be used to release the spring brakes for a short period of time.
You can use the spring brakes to continue driving normally.
The air tanks will automatically refill to a safe air pressure level.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can be used to release the spring brakes for a short period of time.
questions.explanation: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, there is a separate air tank that can temporarily release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. Pushing the proper control will release the spring brakes for a short time so you can move the vehicle in an emergency.
